aspects.says: A participant writes one event per transaction, created in prepare, with the transaction id, the request as a message for the filter to mask, and the reason, logged in finally whatever happened.
basis: section:8.3 One Event per Transaction, Carrying Its Id and the Message Itself

aspects.says: A participant that extends Log gets a logger and realm only when its participant element has a logger attribute; without it its events go nowhere, and without realm they share the realm participant.
basis: section:8.2 A Participant Writes Its Own Event, and Only If Its Element Names a Logger

aspects.says: The TransactionManager's profiler times each participant; ctx.checkPoint goes to the Context's profiler and is invisible without the dump, so a participant times its steps with a Profiler in its own event.
basis: section:8.4 The TransactionManager Times Participants; a Profiler of Your Own Times the Steps

aspects.says: A transaction that never ends writes no event; tail stays at its id while it is the oldest unfinished one, whether or not head moves, and an idle server has tail equal to head.
basis: section:8.5 A Transaction That Never Ends Writes Nothing, and the Ones After It Show Where It Is

aspects.says: A session renames its thread while a participant runs, so SystemMonitor's thread list or a jstack shows the stuck transaction's id, phase, participant and start time.
basis: section:8.5 A Transaction That Never Ends Writes Nothing, and the Ones After It Show Where It Is
aspects.reason: the thread name is read off a monitor's output by a person; a test could only compare a string the page already shows

aspects.says: With the Context dump off, the TransactionManager's event shows each participant's vote but not why; what ctx.log collects is printed only in the dump.
basis: section:8.1 The Transaction Event Says Who Voted, Never Why
